steps.text: Out of the fridge: Sunday's roast chicken (take 175 g her+him of the 600 g batch — see prep notes), Sunday's rice-and-cauliflower, and Sunday's white sauce jar.
Chicken (75/100 g) chopped into rough 2 cm pieces.
Pan, medium-high, rapeseed oil (6/8 g). Chicken in with ½ tsp oregano, ½ tsp cumin, ¼ tsp turmeric and salt. 3 minutes, moving it, until the edges catch.
Rice and cauliflower (55/80 g dry cooked + 130/160 g riced) warmed through — 90 seconds in the microwave, or into the pan for the last minute with a splash of water.
Build: rice base, chicken over, then chickpeas (70/90 g), shredded cabbage (70/80 g) and diced tomato (80/100 g) around the edge. Raw red onion (30/40 g) over.
White sauce from Sunday's jar (50/65 g yoghurt, grated garlic, lemon, a great deal of black pepper). Hot sauce to taste.

why: The spices go on in the pan, not on Sunday. One tray of deliberately plain roast chicken becomes three completely different lunches this week precisely because it was left neutral.
notes: D0-003: the pan-frying oil (single hot-pan use, chicken searing) becomes rapeseed_oil.
D0-003: 'shredded lettuce' in the original step text is explicitly shredded → sweetheart_cabbage.

batchTakeG sums everything drawn from Sunday's prep for this plate: chicken 175 g (of the 600 g roast, 25 g batch headroom — see prep-a.json), dry rice 135 g (of the 320 g batch), riced cauliflower 290 g (of the ~1.4 kg batch), white sauce 115 g (all of Sunday's jar).
